Let $1 \le i < j \le n^2+1$. Since all elements in $S$ are distinct by hypothesis, we have either $x_i < x_j$ or $x_i > x_j$.

	extbf{Case 1 ($x_i < x_j$):} Any increasing subsequence terminating at $x_i$ can be extended by appending $x_j$, yielding an increasing subsequence terminating at $x_j$ of length $a_i + 1$. Consequently, $a_j \ge a_i + 1 > a_i$.

	extbf{Case 2 ($x_i > x_j$):} By identical symmetric reasoning, any decreasing subsequence terminating at $x_i$ can be extended by appending $x_j$, yielding a decreasing subsequence terminating at $x_j$ of length $b_i + 1$. Thus $b_j \ge b_i + 1 > b_i$.
